The wind had finally stopped its restless whispering, and the sea lay flat and silver under the moon. In the tall, white tower at the edge of the cliff, Elias wound the great clockwork mechanism that turned the lighthouse beam. *Click, whir, hum.* The sound was steady and slow, like a heartbeat.

On the railing outside, a single seagull named Pip sat with his wings tucked neatly against his sides. He was tired. He had flown all day, chasing the breeze and skimming the waves, but now the air was still, and his feathers felt heavy with the day’s journey.

Elias opened the door just a crack. The cool night air rushed in, carrying the scent of salt and pine. He didn’t speak, but he poured a small cup of warm tea and set it on the windowsill. Then, he placed a single, smooth pebble next to it—a small gift for the bird who had watched over him all day.

Pip hopped closer. He didn’t drink the tea, of course, but he nudged the pebble gently with his beak, accepting the quiet gesture. He looked up at the great glass lens above, where the light began its slow, sweeping rotation.
